title: Infrared Divergences as Itinerant Vacua
abstract: Infrared divergences (IRDs) are usually treated as pathologies to be cancelled, regularized, or hidden in dressed asymptotic states. This paper develops a complementary and constructive viewpoint: an IRD is the signature of an \emph{itinerant vacuum} -- a quantum vacuum that wanders continuously through a family of inequivalent states as a classical order parameter evolves. Each value of the order parameter carries its own coherent vacuum, so moving the order parameter means traversing a succession of orthogonal vacua. The IRD is the field-theoretic cost of this wandering, and the $1/f$ noise, gravitational memory, and non-Gaussian fluctuations that emerge from it are its observable classical remnants.   The technical core is an exact separation in the real-time closed-time-path (CTP) effective action. The infrared-divergent imaginary part of the influence functional must not be left as a divergent coefficient in a deterministic equation of motion; it is instead converted, by a Hubbard--Stratonovich identity, into a classical stochastic source. This step is an algebraic identity of the generating functional and requires no prior coarse graining or decoherence assumption: the retarded kernel encodes the memory of past vacuum transitions, while the noise kernel encodes the quantum uncertainty of the next one. We apply this construction to four parallel arenas -- soft QED, scalar fields in de Sitter space, soft gravitons, and non-equilibrium phase transitions -- and show that the same itinerant-vacuum mechanism underlies $1/f$ current noise, the primordial power spectrum, gravitational memory, and order-parameter dynamics. A geometric formulation in terms of a Hilbert-space bundle over the vacuum manifold is outlined as an outlook.
summary: This paper reinterprets infrared divergences (IRDs) as the physical signature of an 'itinerant vacuum'—a system continuously moving between distinct quantum states. Using advanced CTP formalism, the authors algebraically convert these divergences into a classical stochastic source term. This framework successfully unifies the origin of phenomena like $1/f$ noise and gravitational memory across diverse fields from QED to cosmology.
main_problem: The paper develops a constructive framework to interpret infrared divergences (IRDs) not as pathologies, but as signatures of an 'itinerant vacuum' undergoing continuous evolution.
main_result: It shows that the IRD can be algebraically converted into a classical stochastic source term within the real-time CTP effective action, unifying the origin of $1/f$ noise and gravitational memory effects.
method: The core method involves using the closed-time-path (CTP) formalism and applying a Hubbard–Stratonovich identity to separate the divergent imaginary part of the influence functional into a classical stochastic source term.
model_or_system: Applications include soft QED, scalar fields in de Sitter space, soft gravitons, and general non-equilibrium phase transitions, all modeled by evolving an order parameter through inequivalent quantum vacua.
key_observables: $1/f$ noise (in current or metric fluctuations), gravitational memory effects, and non-Gaussian fluctuations during phase transitions.
important_parameters: The dynamics are governed by the evolution of a classical order parameter across a manifold of vacuum states.
main_assumptions: The approach requires no prior coarse graining or decoherence assumption; the stochastic source $\xi$ is treated as a c-number average because IR divergences do not depend on $\hbar$.
paper_structure: The paper builds from establishing the concept of the itinerant vacuum, detailing the technical machinery using the CTP effective action and Hubbard–Stratonovich identity, and then applying this unified mechanism to several physical arenas (QED, de Sitter space, gravity).
why_interesting: It provides a powerful, non-perturbative tool for handling low-energy divergences in quantum field theory by mapping them onto observable classical noise sources, which is highly relevant for open quantum systems dynamics.
